blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415: r366's own invented critical-section fix in sub_821FA9E0 clobbered its own return value, causing an unbounded heap overflow; fixed and live-verified). r416/r417 established boot now progresses past sub_821D5F48 and the per-frame loop runs sustained; 'generated entry terminated its own thread' is r277's designed clean-shutdown, not a stall. r418 found presented_frames=0 is pre-existing dead-code wiring (r292, unrelated to r399), and that the real GPU ring (NativeGuestVdService) no longer goes silent after one burst on the r414-fixed binary (a real improvement) but still never emits a Present packet; it also first observed the process taking far longer than its probe window to exit with AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1 enabled. r419 CONFIRMED that slow-exit symptom is real and NOT specific to the trace flag: a plain standalone launch (no gdb, no trace flag) never exits on its own after printing its final diagnostic -- `timeout 60` (SIGTERM only, no -k) did not stop it; killed after ~4 minutes of CPU time. IMPORTANT METHODOLOGY CORRECTION: every 'clean exit' observation in r414-r417 was made under gdb, whose batch-mode `quit` force-kills the inferior at script end regardless of whether it would exit on its own -- none of those captures actually proved self-termination. A /proc thread inventory at the hang shows 8 threads, 3 named after Vulkan driver internals ([vkcf] Analysis, [vkrt] Analysis, [vkps] Update) -- a real Vulkan device/instance is apparently now initialized for the first time in this whole campaign (plausible since boot never got this far before r414), and the working (unverified) hypothesis is that runtime shutdown() does not properly tear down the Vulkan device/instance (vkDeviceWaitIdle/vkDestroyDevice/vkDestroyInstance) before main() returns, leaving the driver's own internal thread pool -- which has no knowledge of this project's guest-thread stop_requested()/GuestThreadTerminated mechanism -- alive forever. Not confirmed by reading native/src/native_vulkan_backend.cpp or by a live attach (gdb -p was refused by this sandbox's yama ptrace_scope policy, not worked around). Whether this hang predates r414 is also unverified (no old binary was relaunched standalone for comparison this cycle) -- the Vulkan-threads-alive observation makes 'unreachable before r414' the more likely explanation than 'a pre-existing bug that was always there but never observed', though this is not proven. Named for r420: read native_vulkan_backend.cpp's destruction sequence and whether shutdown() actually calls it. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool scripts for r413-r419 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
